{"id":"KOD-806","uuid":"e7d4f212-6e76-4d2e-8e0f-792878c654e5","title":"SOLID / DRY / hexagonal / KISS check over the scope layer — which deterministic components encode a fact and which stand in for an agent call","description":"**Outcome:** every deterministic component of the scope layer is reported against the founder's ruling, with evidence, and the founder decides what follows. **This review decides nothing.** It classifies nothing on its own authority, retires nothing, and rewrites no criterion.

**The ruling it serves,** founder 2026-09-09 on <issue id="db886cf4-0bf8-4633-9bb2-3065e12cf87b" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-805/triage-the-codebase-ships-two-opposite-patterns-a-session-does-the">KOD-805</issue>, in full and unqualified:

> *"KISS is always agent call over any manual heuristic."*

**What the review produces.** For each component below: what it does, whether a session with tracker access could do it instead, what would be lost if it did, and what breaks if it is removed — each answer grounded in code read at the trunk and in tests actually run. Then it stops and hands the founder the list. A component is moved, kept or retired only after the founder rules it.

**Components to report on, not a closed list:**

1. The run-event → tracker-state table — 18 kinds, a config table, a boot totality check, one applier seam. Origin was a measured defect: an issue held In Progress 18 days. <issue id="83a0f426-39e1-4636-9e8b-d6e110a965b7" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-750/ruling-which-holder-makes-the-issue-level-state-moves-and-whether-the">KOD-750</issue> made it the sole writer of issue state, and whether it survives is open.
2. `domain/dispatch.py::select_top_ranked` — priority, then oldest-first, then a uniform random draw on an exact tie.
3. `domain/issue_tree.py` — `EmptyFireCriteriaError` and `ScopeSupersessionReadError`, both aborting the whole scope read.
4. The ten exclusion clauses in `domain/dispatch.py`, individually.
5. `domain/topology.py::plan_topology` and its dual blocker rule.

**Observations to TEST, not criteria to apply.** These were written by an automated pass, were wrongly recorded as part of the founder's ruling, and are withdrawn to here. Each is a proposition to confirm or refute; none is a rule, and whether any is a genuine exception is the founder's to rule after the report:

* that a value the tracker already answers is cheaper read than judged;
* that ownership arbitration cannot be a session, because a session asked whether it holds an issue may answer yes twice (<issue id="ebb83291-e57e-4be2-87d6-2b69342a0254" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-747/prevent-a-delayed-claim-renewal-from-reclaiming-ownership-after">KOD-747</issue>);
* that a boot refusal must be deterministic to fail loudly;
* that anything an audit must reproduce identically has to be arithmetic, or two runs cannot be compared.

**Also in scope:** SOLID, DRY and hexagonal, not only KISS. Duplication already observed and worth reporting on — four issue-state vocabularies, two branch-role enums, four three-state verdict enums, and `SessionFailureKind`/`ScanFailureKind` sharing six of seven members.

**Why this blocks.** It blocks work that would build more of what it may report against, so the founder is not asked to rule on a table that has meanwhile grown. It does not block the ownership repair, the walker's composition, or any lane whose subject it does not touch.

**Done when:** the report exists as a comment here, every component above has an entry with its evidence, the four observations are each confirmed or refuted, and the founder has ruled what moves. **Rules:** founder.","priority":{"value":1,"name":"Urgent"},"url":"https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-806/solid-dry-hexagonal-kiss-check-over-the-scope-layer-which","gitBranchName":"rosig-3topase/kod-806-solid-dry-hexagonal-kiss-check-over-the-scope-layer-which","createdAt":"2026-09-09T07:13:50.380Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-12T11:43:31.428Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Todo","statusType":"unstarted","labels":["queue:triage"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"9cb16a46-00ec-4435-a9cd-f8a1535ae634","name":"Todo","type":"unstarted"},"startedAt":"2026-09-09T07:13:50.380Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Goofy","createdById":"998f68f9-58c0-4c31-bdc8-2b9d8da803a2","project":"kodezart v0.3 — scope orchestration","projectId":"91d6fb2e-1be1-4d19-950d-c8e80f3b684e","parentId":"KOD-744","team":"kodezart","teamId":"6a8dcd10-d98b-4bf2-9d37-1f2165b6393a","relations":{"blocks":[{"id":"KOD-797","title":"Ruling: how the plateau and budget put-back is carried as a run-event row"},{"id":"KOD-795","title":"KOD-76-AC-27 — the table carries no vendor state name; the vendor string is resolved at the port boundary"},{"id":"KOD-796","title":"KOD-76-AC-28 — exactly one seam applies a run-event row, and it sits behind the tracker port"},{"id":"KOD-798","title":"Triage: twelve of eighteen run-event kinds are raised by no code and asked for by no criterion"},{"id":"KOD-401","title":"KOD-76-AC-5 — a backwards transition without an explicit permitting row raises a typed error"},{"id":"KOD-403","title":"KOD-76-AC-7 — the table's key set equals the run-event vocabulary, compared in both directions"}],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"KOD-815","title":"Triage: the loop node is not total over FireSpec — run_ralph_loop builds an AuthoredSpec from a generated ticket, so a tracker-native fire cannot reach an iteration"},{"id":"KOD-753","title":"Ruling: the Class row — does hard/soft survive the 2026-09-01 amendments, and the class of KOD-113-AC-3 and KOD-127-AC-6"},{"id":"KOD-163","title":"Port-vocabulary and duplication findings from the 2026-08-31 architecture review"},{"id":"KOD-751","title":"Ruling: who owns the approval barrier that refuses a scope holding an open decision or a Backlog criterion"},{"id":"KOD-787","title":"Ruling: where scope approval is established, and how an unapproved member is made legible"},{"id":"KOD-747","title":"Prevent a delayed claim renewal from reclaiming ownership after another holder acquires"},{"id":"KOD-750","title":"Ruling: which holder makes the issue-level state moves, and whether the run-event → tracker-state table survives"},{"id":"KOD-50","title":"Adopt the scheduled routine prompts (fire prep + grooming) as the behavioral spec for Linear automation"},{"id":"KOD-805","title":"Triage: the codebase ships two opposite patterns — a session does the work, or an engine does — and no ruling says which is which"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

Missing test-backed report work is actionable now; only the final retained/moved/retired component decision is reserved to the founder.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-09-12T11:17:04.377Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-12T11:17:04.298Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"998f68f9-58c0-4c31-bdc8-2b9d8da803a2","name":"Goofy"},"onBehalfOf":null},{"id":"45a07824-b955-473e-919b-67c717b93e12","body":"[architecture review evidence 2026-09-12 · read-only source pass; no fresh test run] This is evidence for the founder decision, not a ruling.

**Run-event → tracker-state table.** Current trunk models it in `OperationConfig` and validates totality/effects, but `TrackerLifecycleWriter` still bypasses it with direct stage writes. KOD-750 has already ruled the table the sole issue-state writer, so the architectural defect is *two authorities*, not merely table complexity. A session could judge what happened, but it cannot replace the deterministic requirement that the same typed event maps to the same tracker transition across adapters/replays. If retained, keep one configured total table and one port-bound applier; remove the parallel lifecycle writer. KOD-797 remains a real representability decision for restore-to-preclaim/budget semantics.

**`domain/dispatch.py::select_top_ranked`.** It computes the operator-declared ordering (domain priority, oldest first, injected draw only on exact equality) and reports the tied set. A session could choose an issue, but replacing this function would lose reproducibility of an explicit scheduling policy and make two identical tracker snapshots legally produce unexplained different priorities. This reads as deterministic policy rather than semantic judgment; if the founder wants agent selection, the ranking contract itself should be retired/amended rather than silently delegated.

**Dispatch clauses inspected.** `clause_in_team`, `clause_in_scope`, `clause_recorded_repository`, `clause_approved`, `clause_open`, `live_blocker`, `clause_unclaimed`, and `clause_undelivered` are direct predicates over port-returned/configured facts. They do not attempt semantic interpretation. Replacing these with a session would trade testable boundary predicates for judgment without adding information. One caveat is approval: the *placement/legibility* policy around scope approval is still open on KOD-787/KOD-751; that decision can change which fact is evaluated where, but it does not make the fact itself semantic.

**`domain/topology.py::plan_topology`.** Pure graph arithmetic: validates complete blocker facts, rejects cycles/missing nodes, propagates effective priority through the blockedBy DAG, and returns ready/blocked sets. A session could propose an order but would lose the equality between the declared blocker graph and the computed ready set, and would make cycle/missing-fact refusal probabilistic. This is a strong example of a deterministic component encoding a fact/policy rather than standing in for a model call.

**`domain/issue_tree.py`.** `index_issue_tree` is structural validation; `SubtreeClosure` defines the gap as the still-open criterion records throughout the subtree; `EmptyFireCriteriaError` refuses a deliverable with no criterion family; `ScopeSupersessionReadError` refuses canceled/duplicate criteria when no native supersession reference is available. The tree/closure arithmetic is reproducible tracker-state interpretation. The *meaning* of whether a criterion is satisfiable belongs in a session; membership/parentage/state/supersession-reference completeness do not.

**Observed counterexample to “agent call over any deterministic component” as a mechanical rewrite rule.** The same review found PR112/PR115 doing the opposite mistake: semantic amendment grounds such as “unsatisfiable at base” are approximated by path/substring/quote mechanics. Those should move toward a structured agent judgment with deterministic evidence/postvalidation. Conversely, topology, ownership, identity, event mapping, exact roster equality, and tracker-native state reads are facts whose reproducibility is part of their contract. The useful cut is therefore not `agent vs code` globally; it is **semantic judgment → typed agent call, invariant/fact/policy arithmetic → deterministic code**. Founder still decides whether that interpretation satisfies the 2026-09-09 KISS ruling.

**DRY/SOLID/hexagonal observations from the initiative review:** current risk is duplicated authority: direct lifecycle writes alongside the event table; `DeliveryCoordinator` name used for union verification while L5 expects a different landing coordinator; `LaneReport` readback shape standing near but not equal to the L6 delivery vector; scope walker implementation not selected by composition. The healing plan should remove/rename these competing authorities before adding new abstractions.

This pass did not execute tests, so it does not close KOD-806's test-backed report requirement. It records the source-grounded component classification needed by the initiative recovery plan.","attachments":[],"createdAt":"2026-09-12T11:03:35.725Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-12T11:03:35.679Z","parentId":null,"resolvedAt":null,"quotedText":null,"author":{"id":"998f68f9-58c0-4c31-bdc8-2b9d8da803a2","name":"Goofy"},"onBehalfOf":null}],"hasNextPage":false}
